rows.subtype: Approach: sees which tasks must finish before others can start [Thinking]
rows.description: A student planning a science exhibition sees that the model cannot be painted before it dries, and that the report needs the results, so those come first.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: maps the longest chain of dependent tasks to see the minimum time [Thinking]
rows.description: A student team charting a project finds that data collection, analysis and report form the longest chain, so any delay there delays everything.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: starts long-lead items early and does small tasks in the gaps [Action]
rows.description: A wedding planner orders the printed cards, which take two weeks, before anything else, and fills waiting time with vendor calls.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path, resource and budget planning

rows.subtype: Approach: focuses on the visible tasks and ignores a hidden dependency [Pitfall]
rows.description: A project team polishes the app screens but forgets that the payment gateway approval takes a month. The launch date slips because of a task nobody had listed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: resource and budget planning
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: redraws the path when a delay appears and shifts resources [Revision]
rows.description: When the approval slips, the lead moves two developers onto the tasks that now determine the end date and lets non-critical items wait.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: critical path
this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A girl washes all her brushes after painting, and puts away all the colours at once, rather than tidying after each colour.

rows.subtype: Approach: groups similar homework into one session [Action]
rows.description: A student does all reading tasks together and then all writing tasks, finding that switching subjects often wastes his time and focus.

rows.subtype: Approach: batches errands into one trip [Thinking]

rows.subtype: Approach: batches emails in fixed slots to protect deep work [Action]

rows.subtype: Approach: batches so long that urgent matters wait too long [Pitfall]
